text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- State airline TAP-Air Portugal would like to form future strategic alliances with Dutch airline KLM and Switzerland's Swissair.
- Subsidiaries of the Antonio Champalimaud group will adopt a common name -- Sottototta, the paper learned from a source close to the group.
- Credito Predial Portugues (CPP) plans to launch two capital increases, boosting the bank's capital to 30 billion escudos.
- Tagus-Gas, seeking the concession to distribute natural gas in the Ribatejo region, will be formally constituted on October 22.
- The Health Ministry owes a record 45 billion escudos to the National Chemists' Association.
- Japonese firm Matsushita and German group Siemens plan to jointly invest around 10 billion escudos in an electronic components factory near Evora in the southern Alentejo region.

- Expresso Atlantico, the new bank created by the partnership between Banco Comercial Portugues and retailer Jeronimo Martins, will start its activities in November. The in-store bank will operate in Jeronimo Martins's hypermarket chain Pingo Doce.
